summary:
--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "The general advice suggests cooperation, forgiveness, avoid retaliation. We should not overfit to given opponents if hidden archive has other strategies."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness and endgame defection. The trace simulates the 12 population opponents and derives best responses, including exploiting cooperative opponents late and defecting against always-defect. It plans an adaptive classifier that cooperates early, punishes defectors, and exploits forgiving opponents at the end.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So a good strategy could be: try to detect if opponent is like slot3 (cooperates regardless of our alternation)." / "So probing is very beneficial!" / "So we should alternate against slot3."
STRATEGY: The parent is a tournament strategy being revised against a population of opponent slots; the trace simulates slot3, slot6, slot9, slot2, slot7, slot1, slot4, slot5, slot0, slot11, slot10, and slot8, and changes the plan to probe with an early D, classify forgivers vs retaliators, then alternate C/D against forgiving opponents while cooperating against retaliators.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the complexity, maybe a robust strategy like 'Tit-for-Tat with forgiveness and endgame defection' is fine. The parent already does that and scored 242.5. We want to improve."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates, retaliates briefly, forgives, and defects in the last few rounds. The trace simulates the 12 opponents (slot0–slot9 etc.) and probes their responses to defection. It changes the strategy by adding a probe phase to detect forgiving opponents (slot3/slot9) and switch to alternating C/D exploitation, while keeping a default TFT-with-forgiveness mode otherwise.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent is similar. The parent scored 242.5. We want to improve." / "The parent only defects at n>=97 and only if coop_rate > 0.7."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like strategy with late endgame exploitation (defects at n>=97 if coop_rate>0.7). Trace simulates probe-based classifier modes (slot3/slot6/slot9/slot1/slot4) and designs a new strategy with early probes, high-exploit alternating mode, and default retaliator/slot6 modes. Changes: more aggressive endgame defection, periodic defections to keep C rate below 85%, and probe-based mode switching.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the time, I'll implement this strategy. It's complex but should be better than parent."
STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional strategy that probes with C,D,C,D,C, then branches on opponent's r3/r5 actions into retaliator, high-exploit, or cautious/slot6 modes. The trace simulates slot0, slot3, slot6, slot7, slot8, slot9, slot11, and retaliators against the probe sequence. It changes the parent by adding nested helper functions, periodic defection, endgame defection, and mode selection based on early opponent responses.
